name: Stable SelectionArea participant-order fast path

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: headed WASM/WebGPU SelectionArea fixture at DPR 1 and DPR 2
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Stable participant-order fast path

Avoid materializing participant IDs and membership sets when the current and next traversals have the same length and the same selectable IDs in order. Preserve the existing membership-set path whenever that direct comparison detects a change.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement plan

Use the completed 16 baseline for the unchanged many-participant fixture, then measure the same headed WASM/WebGPU SelectionArea fixture at DPR 1 and DPR 2 with 35 repetitions per project and five warmups discarded. Retain the change only if p95 does not regress more than five percent and the focused fixture remains correct.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected outcome

An unchanged SelectionArea frame creates no participant ID vectors or participant-sized temporary `HashSet`s. Reordered, added, and removed participants continue through the established membership comparison, preserving all selection semantics.

measurements.target: headed WASM/WebGPU SelectionArea fixture; 35 repetitions per DPR with five warmups discarded

reportMarkdown:
## Stable SelectionArea participant-order fast path

Accepted. `SelectionAreaState::end_frame` first compares the current and next participant sequences directly. When they are identical, no participant ID vectors or temporary membership `HashSet`s are created. A changed sequence retains the established set comparison to preserve membership semantics.

The focused WASM/WebGPU fixture passed at DPR 1 and DPR 2, then passed 70 repeated runs. Input-to-published-frame p50/p95 was 92.52/96.55 ms at DPR 1 versus the 88.19/95.91 ms baseline, and 90.84/98.86 ms at DPR 2 versus 89.56/106.01 ms. The small DPR 1 p95 variation remains below the five-percent rejection threshold; DPR 2 p95 improved. A fresh DPR 1 screenshot retains the expected participant rendering after the scroll action.

Decision: retain the direct stable-order check. It is the smallest way to remove dormant participant-sized allocations without adding map-maintenance work to every traversal.
